title: Offence
description: A crime as the state’s law defines it (D46, D47, D82): what it covers, the most it carries, and what a court imposes. The figures trace to CALIBRATION.md.

under.description: It covers goods worth less than this, in cents. Left out for an offence that goes by weight, or covers any value.

priors.description: It covers someone with at most this many prior convictions.

days.description: The most days in jail or prison it carries.

fineMax.description: The most it carries as a fine, in cents, or timesValue times the value if that is more.

fine.description: The fine a court in the slice imposes on a conviction, in cents (tune).

costs.description: Court costs and assessments on a conviction, in cents (tune).

grams.description: For a controlled substance: it covers less than this weight, in tenths of a gram, of any mixture holding it (D82).

felony.description: A felony, which a record shows as one, and which can be served in prison (D81). A misdemeanour when left out.

deferral.description: A first offence can be deferred: HYTA under its age, probation and no public record (D47, D82).

first.description: A felony's sentence for someone with no conviction before: days in jail, then days on probation (D82). Within the sentencing guidelines' range for the offence's class with no prior record.

repeat.description: A felony's sentence for someone with a conviction before: months in prison, served as days (D81).
